metadata.source: Compiled from agricultural extension services, USDA, and peer-reviewed phytopathology literature

symptoms.mild: Small olive-green to brown spots on leaves, slight leaf curling at edges
symptoms.moderate: Dark, velvety lesions covering 20-50% of leaf surface, premature yellowing
symptoms.severe: Extensive black scabby lesions, heavy defoliation, fruit cracking and deformation

prevention: Apply fungicide at green tip stage
Monitor weather for infection periods (Mills table)

symptoms.mild: Small yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
symptoms.moderate: Raised orange pustules on leaf undersides, spots enlarging to 5-10mm
symptoms.severe: Extensive orange-red lesions with tube-like structures, premature leaf drop, fruit infection

cultural: Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts within 2-mile radius

prevention: Apply fungicide from tight cluster through 2nd cover
Scout for galls on junipers in spring

symptoms.mild: Small, water-soaked spots on leaves, slightly raised
symptoms.moderate: Dark brown to black angular lesions with yellow halos, 3-5mm diameter
symptoms.severe: Extensive leaf blight, defoliation over 50%, fruit lesions (raised scab-like)

cultural: Rotate to non-solanaceous crops for 2 years
Use drip irrigation to avoid wetting foliage

prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Hot water seed treatment (125F for 25 min)

symptoms.mild: Small rectangular tan-gray lesions between leaf veins
symptoms.moderate: Elongated gray lesions 2-5cm, parallel to veins, covering 25-50% of leaf
symptoms.severe: Coalescent lesions causing entire leaf blight, premature plant death

prevention: Apply fungicide if weather favors disease at VT-R1

symptoms.mild: Elongated elliptical gray-green lesions 2-5cm on lower leaves
symptoms.moderate: Cigar-shaped lesions 5-15cm, gray-green turning tan, spreading to upper canopy
symptoms.severe: Massive lesion coverage causing complete leaf necrosis, significant yield loss

cultural: Crop rotation with soybeans or small grains
Plant resistant hybrids with Ht genes

prevention: Apply fungicide when lesions reach ear leaf
Choose hybrids with multiple Ht resistance genes

symptoms.mild: Small circular to elongated cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
symptoms.moderate: Numerous pustules coalescing, dark reddish-brown spore masses, chlorotic halos
symptoms.severe: Dense pustule coverage, premature leaf senescence, secondary infections

biological: Generally not economically necessary for common rust
cultural: Early planting to avoid late-season spore pressure

prevention: Monitor for pustule development starting at V10
Fungicide only if severe before tasseling

symptoms.mild: Tan circular leaf spots with dark brown margins, 2-10mm
symptoms.moderate: Numerous leaf spots with black pycnidia visible, early fruit infection (brown spots)
symptoms.severe: Berries shrivel to hard black mummies, widespread canopy infection

cultural: Prune for air circulation and sunlight penetration

prevention: Begin fungicide applications at 10-inch shoot growth
Critical spray period: bloom through 4 weeks post-bloom

symptoms.mild: Small dark brown spots with concentric rings (target-spot pattern) on older leaves
symptoms.moderate: Enlarging lesions with prominent concentric rings, lower leaf yellowing and drop
symptoms.severe: Extensive defoliation starting from bottom, stem lesions, tuber infection (dark sunken spots)

cultural: 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops

prevention: Begin fungicide at row closure or first symptoms
Harvest mature tubers to avoid skin injury

symptoms.mild: Water-soaked irregular pale green spots at leaf tips and edges
symptoms.moderate: Dark brown-black lesions expanding rapidly, white cottony sporangia on undersides in humid conditions
symptoms.severe: Entire plant collapse within days, foul-smelling tuber rot, devastating field-wide losses

cultural: Hill tubers to prevent spore wash to tubers

prevention: Use certified seed from disease-free sources
Apply protectant fungicides before disease onset

symptoms.mild: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves
symptoms.moderate: Target-spot lesions enlarge, yellow halos form, lower third of plant defoliated
symptoms.severe: Extensive defoliation, stem cankers, fruit calyx-end rot with dark leathery lesions

cultural: Stake and prune for air movement

prevention: Rotate out of tomato/potato for 3 years
Begin sprays at first fruit set

symptoms.mild: Irregularly shaped water-soaked gray-green spots on leaves
symptoms.moderate: Large dark brown-black blotches, white mold on undersides, stem streaking
symptoms.severe: Rapid plant collapse, brown greasy fruit rot, entire crop loss possible within a week

cultural: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately

prevention: Apply fungicide before wet weather forecasts

symptoms.mild: Small circular spots (1-3mm) with dark borders and gray centers on lower leaves
symptoms.moderate: Numerous spots coalescing, tiny black pycnidia visible in centers, progressive defoliation upward
symptoms.severe: Near-complete defoliation, fruit sunscald from exposure, significant yield loss

chemical: Chlorothalonil every 7-10 days during wet weather
cultural: Stake or cage plants for airflow

symptoms.mild: Small dark water-soaked spots on leaves, greasy appearance
symptoms.moderate: Angular brown-black lesions with yellow halos, spots on stems and petioles
symptoms.severe: Widespread defoliation, raised scab-like spots on fruit, major quality loss

prevention: Use pathogen-free seed (hot water treat at 122F for 25 min)

symptoms.mild: Light and dark green mosaic pattern on young leaves
symptoms.moderate: Leaf distortion, fern-like appearance, reduced leaf size, uneven ripening of fruit
symptoms.severe: Severe stunting, shoestring leaves, fruit with internal browning, major yield loss

chemical: No chemical cure for viral diseases
cultural: Disinfect hands and tools with milk or 10% bleach

prevention: Wash hands with soap before handling plants

symptoms.mild: Slight upward curling of leaf margins, mild yellowing of new growth
symptoms.moderate: Pronounced upward cupping and yellowing of leaves, stunted growth, flower drop
symptoms.severe: Severe stunting, thick leathery yellow leaves, minimal or no fruit set

chemical: No cure; manage whitefly vector with imidacloprid or cyantraniliprole

prevention: Install yellow sticky traps for whitefly monitoring

symptoms.mild: Pale green-yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces, olive-green mold on lower surfaces
symptoms.moderate: Spots enlarge, dense olive-brown velvety mold underneath, leaves curl upward
symptoms.severe: Extensive leaf browning and desiccation, fruit infection rare but possible

aliases: Tomato two spotted spider mites leaf

symptoms.mild: Fine stippling (tiny yellow dots) on upper leaf surfaces
symptoms.moderate: Leaves turn bronze-yellow, fine webbing visible between leaves, stippling becomes dense
symptoms.severe: Extensive webbing, leaf desiccation and drop, plant dieback in severe infestations

cultural: Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies

prevention: Scout weekly with hand lens on leaf undersides
Maintain adequate irrigation (drought stress promotes mites)

symptoms.mild: Small white powdery spots on upper leaf surfaces
symptoms.moderate: White powder covers majority of leaf surface, leaves yellow at margins
symptoms.severe: Entire leaf surface coated, leaves brown and die, reduced fruit quality and sunscald

prevention: Apply fungicide at first sign of disease

environmental_risk.rainfall: low, warm humid air but dry leaf surface

symptoms.mild: Small dark purple spots on upper leaf surfaces
symptoms.moderate: Spots enlarge with dark purple borders, centers may fall out creating shot-holes
symptoms.severe: Leaves appear scorched and brown at margins, heavy defoliation weakens plants

chemical: Captan at renovation and in fall
cultural: Renovate beds after harvest (mow and thin)
Improve air circulation with proper spacing

symptoms.mild: Small angular brown spots between veins (brown spot) or circular spots with gray centers (frogeye)
symptoms.moderate: Spots coalesce, inter-veinal necrosis, premature yellowing of lower canopy
symptoms.severe: Early defoliation, pod infection, significant yield reduction

cultural: Rotate with corn or small grains
Plant resistant varieties for frogeye (Rcs3 gene)

prevention: Apply fungicide if disease severity exceeds threshold at R3

symptoms.mild: Small purple-red spots on upper leaf surface
symptoms.moderate: Spots turn brown with white spore masses on undersides, yellowing around lesions
symptoms.severe: Heavy defoliation by midsummer, weakened trees susceptible to winter injury

biological: Copper sprays at early leaf stage

prevention: Apply fungicide from petal fall through harvest
Maintain tree vigor with proper nutrition

symptoms.mild: Slight puckering and reddening of young expanding leaves
symptoms.moderate: Leaves thickened, curled, and distorted with red-yellow coloration, white spore coating
symptoms.severe: Severe defoliation in spring, fruit drop, tree weakening if repeated years

cultural: Apply one dormant spray — disease cannot be controlled once symptoms appear

prevention: MUST spray before bud swell in late winter
One well-timed spray prevents all infection

symptoms.mild: Small dark spots on leaves, minor cane lesions
symptoms.moderate: Leaf spots enlarge, gray centers develop, cane lesions deepen
symptoms.severe: Extensive leaf spotting and drop, deep cane cankers, fruit quality loss

cultural: Prune out old floricanes after harvest

prevention: Apply dormant spray before bud break

symptoms.mild: Small reddish-brown spots on leaves in early summer
symptoms.moderate: Spots enlarge, centers turn gray-brown, premature reddening of leaves
symptoms.severe: Heavy defoliation, reduced fruit bud formation for next year

prevention: Apply fungicide after harvest through fall
Maintain plant vigor with proper fertilization

symptoms.mild: N/A — plant is healthy
symptoms.moderate: N/A — plant is healthy
symptoms.severe: N/A — plant is healthy
